title: Deference to Grovelling: Yielding, Then Losing Your Dignity
core: All of these describe placing yourself below someone else — letting their judgment, wishes, or vanity outrank your own. The scale runs from a respectful half-step back to crawling: how much self-respect is surrendered, whether the yielding is a settled condition or a performance, and whether the speaker admires it or is disgusted by it. Only the first is something you would say about yourself; the rest are verdicts delivered from outside, by a watcher who thinks less of the person doing it.
exam_note: The trap is the first-vs-rest split: **deference** is neutral-to-flattering while everything after it is contemptuous, so GRE sentences signal with a single evaluative word ("merely," "sickening," "to his credit") — read the clue for whether the writer approves before picking.

words.nuance: The only member here that leaves your dignity intact — the yielding is chosen, bounded, and usually to your credit. Watch the frame **in deference to**, which means "out of respect for" a person's grief, expertise, or seniority, not "in submission to" their power.

Names a settled condition, not a performance: this person has stopped having judgment of their own, and there is no flattery or angle in it. It also indicts the one on top — a subservient staff implies a domineering boss — and uniquely among these it works on things (*form subservient to function*).

The pleasing is strategic. The word smells of self-interest — the fawner wants the promotion, the tip, the favour — so it attaches to the smiling yes-man and the courtier, not to the merely spineless. The most formal and literary word in the group.

The bodily, doglike version: gushing, hovering, laughing too hard, praise poured on a specific admired or powerful person. Needs its preposition — you fawn **over** or **on** someone — and unlike **obsequious** it can be pure infatuation with no payoff in mind (fans fawn over a celebrity).

The floor of the scale, and the only one built on physical abasement — crawling face-down. It's aimed at begging or apologising, typically after you've done something wrong or need a favour granted, so it's transactional and episodic where **subservient** is chronic.
